answer: Peer-graded work can be made sybil-resistant by tying voting weight to a vesting bond that unlocks only after consecutive honest epochs, with the wait itself stretching in a spiral as more keys appear from the same funding source. A grove of sockpuppets then starves: each clone locks capital, but their unseasoned attestations never clear the reef that established graders must cross before a grade or vote counts. Mass identity farming becomes a capital trap rather than a shortcut.
